title: Paloma and the Scholarship
premise: Elodie Almeida, the invisible statistician of his elite prep school's championship basketball team, has spent four years documenting the scholarship system that quietly funnels spots to donors' children. When the college essay prompt asks students to name a truth they've never said aloud, Elodie writes about the rigged game — and the essay leaks, threatening the coach, the headmaster, and the scholarship of his best friend Marcus, the team's star. To protect Marcus and expose the corruption without destroying the season, Elodie must turn his data into testimony, rally the found family he never admitted he had, and win the state championship as leverage. In the end the team loses by two points, but Elodie's testimony forces an investigation; Marcus keeps his scholarship through a newly created merit fund, and Elodie finally signs his own name to something true.
about_author: Dominic Joubert is a former high school math teacher from Lyon who spent six years coaching quiz bowl before turning to fiction full-time. He writes stories about quiet kids who keep score.

chapters.title: The Counting House
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. We meet him in the stats booth above the gym, tracking shot charts for a team that never learns his name, counting down 212 days to graduation. He reveals his private spreadsheet: which scholarships went where, and why. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: One Honest Question
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The college essay prompt lands in every senior's inbox: 'Name a truth you've never said aloud.' Elodie drafts his answer at 2 a.m. — the rigged scholarship ledger — then deletes it. His friend Priya finds the draft on a shared drive. Beat: the first crack in invisibility.

chapters.title: Marcus's Two Futures
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Marcus, the star forward whose scholarship depends on staying silent about the booster scandal both boys have half-noticed. Marcus begs Elodie to let it go; Elodie realizes Marcus knew more than he let on. Beat: loyalty tested before the stakes are even clear.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The essay spreads through the school after a misdirected email. Coach Delacroix pulls Elodie into an office where threats arrive dressed as concern. The headmaster offers Elodie a 'legacy grant' — hush money shaped like a gift. Beat: fear, and the seduction of being finally seen.

chapters.title: What the Data Says
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie audits three years of admissions records and finds the pattern is worse than he thought — and that Priya's older brother was one of its casualties. He decides not to retract. Beat: grief converting into resolve.

chapters.title: The Team That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs in short vignettes. The squad fragments: some players side with the boosters, some with Marcus, some just want to play. A midnight practice, no coaches, becomes the moment the ragged group chooses each other. Beat: found family assembling itself out of conflict.

chapters.title: Delacroix's Ledger
chapters.summary: Coach Delacroix's POV, sympathetic and damning. We see how a decent man became the machine's face, and watch him destroy evidence while telling himself it's mercy. He suspends Elodie from the stats booth. Beat: the banality of complicity.

chapters.title: Playoffs, Uninvited
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Barred from official duties, Elodie works from the bleachers with a notebook while the team plays the semifinal short-handed. They win ugly. Afterward, a journalist contacts Priya: someone inside the school is feeding her the story — and it isn't Elodie. Beat: hope with a hook in it.

chapters.title: The Championship That Matters
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. State final: tied with seconds left, Marcus passes instead of shooting, trusting the play Elodie scribbled on a napkin. They lose by two. In the empty locker room, Elodie goes public anyway, reading his essay to teammates and phones alike. Beat: climax — defeat and truth-telling at once.

chapters.title: Signed, Elodie Almeida
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, weeks later. The investigation opens; Delacroix resigns; the merit fund saves Marcus. Elodie submits his college application unchanged, real name attached, and visits the empty stats booth one last time — leaving the door unlocked for whoever counts next. Beat: resolution, quiet and earned.
